north_star: Build a modular, inspectable, multilingual semantic representation and reasoning system that converts language input into traceable semantic structures, preserves uncertainty, and supports bounded knowledge retrieval and evidence-grounded reasoning. Grow capability through small independently evaluated increments rather than through unverified breadth or a monolithic model.

target_architecture.name: Input and source preservation
target_architecture.purpose: Preserve exact bytes/text, language profile, source spans, source identity, transformations, and rights/provenance before interpretation.

target_architecture.name: Segmentation and lexical analysis
target_architecture.purpose: Produce token, lemma, morphology, POS, and sense candidates while preserving OOVs, ambiguity, and source evidence.

target_architecture.name: Syntax and construction analysis
target_architecture.purpose: Build versioned construction, attachment, dependency, and argument-structure candidates with alternatives.

target_architecture.name: Semantic composition
target_architecture.purpose: Compose typed predicates, roles, participants, properties, relations, events, states, and modifiers without losing source grounding.

target_architecture.name: Operators and discourse
target_architecture.purpose: Represent negation, quantification, tense, aspect, modality, conditionals, scope, mentions, reference candidates, and discourse context.

target_architecture.name: Canonical projection and persistence
target_architecture.purpose: Project only representable meaning into versioned USG-SEM contracts; preserve unprojectable material explicitly; use the existing SQLite authority.

target_architecture.name: Knowledge and retrieval
target_architecture.purpose: Retrieve provenance-bearing candidate knowledge through versioned read-only adapters; distinguish forms, senses, concepts, classes, instances, and assertions.

target_architecture.name: Reasoning and explanation
target_architecture.purpose: Apply explicit rules with typed inputs, preconditions, derivations, evidence, conflict handling, bounded execution, and explanations.

target_architecture.name: Evaluation and diagnostics
target_architecture.purpose: Measure stage reliability and semantic quality separately across frozen, synthetic, controlled, and naturalistic populations.

target_architecture.name: Development intelligence and governed growth
target_architecture.purpose: Connect failures to proposals, candidate sandboxes, independent evaluation, acceptance, replay, monitoring, and rollback.

invariants: USG-SEM/1.0 remains normative and unchanged unless a separately versioned migration is explicitly approved.
The existing SQLite canonical document store remains the only canonical document authority; indexes and caches remain rebuildable.
JavaScript Workbench, Python kernel, Python interpreter, adapters, and native packages remain separate implementation lines until common conformance tests demonstrate specific equivalence.
Lexical, morphology, parser, and semantic discoveries remain candidates until their own acceptance and integration decisions pass.
A schema-valid graph, model-generated answer, cross-runtime agreement, or successful workflow does not prove semantic correctness.
Unknown, ambiguous, conflicting, unsupported, and unprojectable content must remain explicit; abstention is preferable to invented certainty.
Naturalistic, synthetic, randomized, controlled-diagnostic, historical, and external-candidate populations must not be pooled without a defensible common denominator.
Every accepted result must identify code commit, resource versions/digests, language profile, population, evaluation method, and limitations.
No single intelligence, AGI, or universal-understanding score is used as an acceptance criterion.
Autonomous automation may collect, diagnose, prioritize, test, and propose; semantic runtime promotion remains behind explicit gates.
future_phase_policy: Future phase numbers and titles are planning labels, not accepted scope or permission to start implementation. Re-cut or split a proposed phase when evidence shows that its work is too broad, dependencies changed, or a smaller independently acceptable increment is safer. Do not create a new phase to avoid an existing continuation tracker or migration obligation.

phases.title: Cross-runtime conformance and reproducible evaluation foundation
phases.objective: Make every implementation's behavior comparable on the same frozen inputs, profiles, normalized outputs, and replayable cases. Establish what actually works in each implementation before expanding semantic breadth.

work_items.title: Define the shared conformance fixture contract
work_items.objective: Specify common case IDs, source text, language profile, feature scope, expected evidence, normalized semantic output, ambiguity/abstention expectations, and provenance.
implementation_sequence: Inspect USG-SEM/1.0, Phase 4/5 envelopes, JS Workbench v0.5.4, Python kernel v0.7.0, and existing browser runner.
Define a versioned fixture JSON schema; do not force unlike internal objects into a false common shape.
Include input, profile, capabilities under test, expected spans, expected normalized nodes/relations, allowed alternatives, and explicit non-claims.
Create fixtures for capabilities already shared by at least two implementations.
acceptance: Schema validates all fixtures.
Fixture IDs and source/resource provenance are stable.
Unsupported features are explicitly marked and cannot be counted as failures of an implementation that does not claim support.

work_items.title: Normalize execution reports without erasing implementation differences
work_items.objective: Provide a per-implementation normalized result envelope that retains native payload references and version metadata.
implementation_sequence: Define normalizers for spans, lexical candidates, constructions, roles, operators, discourse links, unresolved items, diagnostics, and abstention.
Preserve native implementation identifiers as opaque references; compare semantic content rather than local IDs.
Record implementation commit, resource digest, runner version, language profile, and execution outcome.
Add invalid/missing-field and lossy-normalization tests.
acceptance: Round-trip references to native payloads are retained.
No normalizer silently drops ambiguity or unsupported content.
Normalizer conformance fixtures pass for each registered target.

work_items.title: Build the common multi-runtime runner
work_items.objective: Run the same fixture set separately against each declared runtime and collect deterministic reports.
implementation_sequence: Create a target registry with entry point, supported profiles/features, command, timeout, environment, and artifact contract.
Run JS in the browser adapter and Python implementations in isolated processes.
Separate target-not-supported, not-configured, skipped, crashed, timed-out, invalid-output, and semantic mismatch outcomes.
Persist per-case raw and normalized outputs.
acceptance: All runnable targets execute reproducibly on the same selected fixture IDs.
Unconfigured/unsupported targets are never reported as successful tests.
Case, target, attempt, and scenario counts reconcile.

work_items.title: Publish a capability-by-runtime conformance matrix
work_items.objective: Show which feature/profile combinations are implemented, tested, conformant, not tested, unsupported, or blocked.
implementation_sequence: Populate rows by implementation, version, language profile, construction, and semantic feature.
Link each cell to exact fixtures, reports, commits, and resource digests.
Use statuses that distinguish component-tested from cross-runtime conformant.
Add a regression that prevents matrix cells from becoming conformant without exact shared-run evidence.
acceptance: Every claim has evidence links and precise scope.
Agreement is not labelled semantic truth.
The matrix can be refreshed automatically from runner artifacts.

work_items.title: Unify stage-level diagnostic and failure attribution
work_items.objective: Connect the first supported blocker, parallel blockers, downstream incomplete stages, and resource dependencies across implementations.
implementation_sequence: Reuse Phase 4/5 dependency graphs and diagnostic codes where their semantics match.
Add explicit mapping tables for implementation-specific diagnostics; leave unmapped codes unmapped.
Report first blocker separately from correlated downstream symptoms.
Link every ranked finding to a replayable case and exact source/resource versions.
acceptance: Attribution is profile-specific and does not impose a false global pipeline order.
Unknown diagnostic mappings remain visible.
Every high-priority failure cluster has exact reproducer cases.

work_items.title: Establish deterministic replay and regression gates
work_items.objective: Make every accepted fix reproducible and protect prior bounded capabilities.
implementation_sequence: Pin fixture set, expected outputs, resources, normalizer, and runner versions.
Define volatile-field allowlists rather than ignoring arbitrary output differences.
Run replay on pull requests touching covered stages/resources.
Publish before/after deltas and reject unapproved baseline edits.
acceptance: Prior accepted cases replay on exact PR head.
Baseline updates require separate rationale and evidence.
Any regression in protected scope blocks merge.

exit_gate: Shared fixture schema and normalized outputs are versioned.
At least one explicitly scoped cross-runtime fixture set runs on every eligible implementation.
Capability matrix and failure reports are generated from exact run artifacts.
Counts, unsupported states, and semantic correctness claims remain separate.
No runtime behavior is broadened solely to satisfy conformance.
guardrails: No forced equivalence between distinct implementations.
No cross-runtime agreement claim without common fixtures.
No accepted semantic scope expansion in this phase.

phases.title: Independent evaluation and language evidence programme
phases.objective: Create trustworthy, rights-aware, population-specific evaluation resources so future semantic expansion can be measured without self-validation or data leakage.

work_items.title: Create a versioned corpus and evidence registry
work_items.objective: Record source, license, language/profile, retrieval date, transformations, privacy screening, population type, annotation status, and allowed use for every evaluation corpus.
implementation_sequence: Inventory current PUD, synthetic, randomized, controlled, historical, and candidate datasets.
Preserve translated Arabic PUD as translated input; do not label it native conversational Arabic.
Add source manifests and immutable content digests.
Reject unknown rights for redistribution or automated use unless separately reviewed.
acceptance: Every corpus has machine-readable provenance and use restrictions.
No dataset is silently copied or relabelled.
Population types remain separate in metrics and reports.

work_items.title: Complete and characterize the naturalistic pilot
work_items.objective: Measure real-text input coverage and failure patterns without claiming semantic gold where none exists.
implementation_sequence: Run the registered English and Arabic PUD pilot at its declared sample size.
Report source composition, duplicates, language limitations, transformation/translation status, and sampling seed.
Add domain and sentence-length stratification where reliable.
Report end-to-end completion and unsupported/ambiguous outcomes, not semantic accuracy.
acceptance: Full scheduled campaign artifact exists and is reproducible.
Naturalistic input-only metrics are separate from synthetic and controlled results.
Arabic translation limitation is displayed in every summary.

work_items.title: Define independent annotation and adjudication protocol
work_items.objective: When semantic gold is needed, define labels, evidence requirements, disagreement, adjudication, and annotator independence.
implementation_sequence: Write a construction-specific annotation manual before annotation.
Specify whether labels cover spans, morphology, syntax, semantic roles, relations, operators, or discourse.
Record independent annotator decisions and adjudication provenance where human labeling is used.
If no rights-cleared independent gold is available, keep claims synthetic/structural and do not invent human-like gold.
acceptance: Annotation guidelines are versioned and tested on pilot examples.
Independent and adjudicated labels are distinguishable.
Unresolvable disagreements remain unresolved, not overwritten.

work_items.title: Create leak-resistant train/development/test partitions
work_items.objective: Prevent candidate generators and grammar tuning from learning from final evaluation examples.
implementation_sequence: Split by source/document and near-duplicate clusters, not random sentence only.
Freeze a held-out test manifest and digest.
Allow a development set for rule tuning and a separate acceptance set for final evaluation.
Add automated overlap/leakage checks across resources, candidate generation, and test fixtures.
acceptance: Held-out cases are inaccessible to candidate-generation steps by policy.
Leakage tests pass.
Any split replacement creates a new version and documented migration.

work_items.title: Define capability-specific metric cards
work_items.objective: Report execution reliability, span integrity, lexical recall/precision, syntax attachment, role/relation correctness, operator scope, discourse linking, abstention calibration, and end-to-end semantic accuracy separately.
implementation_sequence: Define numerator, denominator, exclusions, and population for every metric.
Separate candidate inclusion from correct disambiguation.
Report per-language, per-construction, and per-domain results.
Use confidence intervals where sampling supports them; do not fabricate estimates for small or non-random samples.
acceptance: Every metric has an explicit denominator and interpretation boundary.
No universal aggregate intelligence score exists.
Synthetic exact-oracle and naturalistic input-only metrics are clearly distinguished.

work_items.title: Create per-construction acceptance profiles
work_items.objective: Make each new construction independently acceptable by language and scope.
implementation_sequence: Define positive, negative, ambiguous, boundary, adversarial, and minimal-pair cases.
Declare required exact spans, roles/relations, allowed alternatives, and abstention behavior.
Define thresholds before running the held-out set.
Require prior accepted regression suites to remain green.
acceptance: No aggregate score can hide failure in a supported language/profile.
Thresholds and fixtures are frozen before final run.
Acceptance report lists exact feature boundary and exclusions.

exit_gate: Corpus rights/provenance registry is complete for the resources used.
Naturalistic pilot has a reproducible population-specific result.
Independent annotation policy and held-out protocol exist.
Metric definitions and acceptance profiles are versioned.
No synthetic or input-only result is misrepresented as independent semantic gold.

phases.title: Lexical, morphology, and contextual candidate quality
phases.objective: Turn external lexical acquisition into a high-quality, ambiguity-preserving candidate evidence service that can support downstream interpretation without becoming an unreviewed runtime dictionary.

work_items.title: Stabilize source-specific lexical ingestion
work_items.objective: Normalize source records while preserving original form, lemma, sense, language, source locator, license, retrieval time, and digest.
implementation_sequence: Audit crawler checkpoint, manifest, shard identity, retries, duplicate handling, and storage budget.
Keep source-native records and normalized candidate records linked but separate.
Add per-provider quality and rights states.
Make incremental ingestion deterministic and resumable.
acceptance: Shard inventory matches manifest and no conflicting duplicate batches exist.
Every normalized record links to immutable source evidence.
Missing/unknown rights remain blocked from disallowed use.

work_items.title: Improve morphology candidate generation
work_items.objective: Build language-profile-specific morphological alternatives and mappings with explicit source-tag uncertainty.
implementation_sequence: Audit the current zero-overlap/low-coverage PUD morphology results and source-tag mapping assumptions.
Define feature bundles and mapping confidence per language profile.
Add candidate generation for inflectional forms with exact surface/lemma links.
Evaluate against pinned UPOS and morphology populations.
acceptance: Candidate precision/recall reported by language and tag.
Unmapped tags stay explicit.
No morphology candidate is called an accepted parse.

work_items.title: Integrate lexical candidates through the versioned adapter
work_items.objective: Expose lemma, POS, sense, morphology, provenance, and ambiguity to interpretation stages as candidates.
implementation_sequence: Reuse USG-LEXICAL-CANDIDATES and the existing adapter rather than add a parallel vocabulary store.
Add adapter versions to interpreter run envelopes.
Allow consumers to request candidate sets with bounded retrieval limits.
Keep candidate lifecycle and runtime resource lifecycle separate.
acceptance: OOV and polysemy regressions remain green.
Every candidate has provenance and stable identity.
No forced single POS or sense is returned when evidence is insufficient.

work_items.title: Add contextual ranking as a non-authoritative candidate ranker
work_items.objective: Use surrounding syntax, domain, morphology, and context to order candidates without silently converting rank into semantic truth.
implementation_sequence: Establish unigram/frequency baseline and existing HMM diagnostic baseline.
Benchmark contextual alternatives on held-out ambiguity cases.
Expose ranked alternatives, feature contributions, and confidence calibration.
Require abstention when candidate margins/evidence are inadequate.
acceptance: Held-out results outperform the baseline on declared metrics without unacceptable language regression.
Ranking never changes candidate identity or source evidence.
No runtime promotion occurs until separately accepted.

work_items.title: Build lexical candidate lifecycle and promotion evaluation
work_items.objective: Define how source candidates become validated-for-profile, accepted runtime resources, deprecated, or rejected.
implementation_sequence: Define lifecycle transitions and required evidence.
Require held-out lexical/morphology evaluation plus downstream regression replay.
Compare retrieval precision, OOV reduction, false candidate inclusion, and ambiguity preservation.
Issue a separate versioned integration proposal per resource family.
acceptance: Candidate-to-runtime transitions are auditable and reversible.
No source-count or crawl-completion metric alone can authorize promotion.
Resource rollback is tested.

exit_gate: Current external shard set is inventoried and rights-labelled.
Morphology and lexical candidates are evaluated separately from runtime semantics.
Adapter preserves ambiguity, identity, and provenance.
Any proposed runtime resource has held-out evidence and a rollback plan.

phases.title: Construction grammar and syntactic coverage expansion
phases.objective: Expand the interpreter through small, frequent, independently testable constructions selected from real failure evidence and available evaluation support.

work_items.title: Choose construction increments by measured value
work_items.objective: Rank candidate constructions by recurrence, supported-language demand, resource readiness, expected benefit, evaluation readiness, and implementation cost.
implementation_sequence: Group Open-World and naturalistic failures by construction and first blocking stage.
Check existing Phase 6 continuation IDs before creating new work.
Choose one construction per implementation increment; publish exclusions and reasons.
Require a gold/evaluation path before enabling semantic output.
acceptance: Selection rationale links to exact cases and evidence populations.
No new phase duplicates Phase 6 continuation.
Each construction has a bounded profile.

work_items.title: Expand nominal, property, possession, and modifier semantics
work_items.objective: Extend beyond accepted synthetic profiles only where exact construction evidence supports the additional relation.
implementation_sequence: Review Phase 6 nominal/property/possession/modifier definitions and continuation records.
Add one relation/construction at a time with role, direction, scope, and span rules.
Preserve ambiguous attachment and omitted arguments.
Use a versioned candidate extension until the gate passes.
acceptance: Positive/negative/ambiguous/boundary fixtures pass per language.
Property, possession, and modifier relations are not conflated.
Canonical projection remains lossless or explicitly opaque.

work_items.title: Expand coordination, embedding, subordinate and relative clauses
work_items.objective: Handle broader clause attachment and argument-gap constructions with explicit attachment alternatives.
implementation_sequence: Start from P6-CONT-01/02 and accepted Phase 5/6 profiles.
Add complement, relative, conditional, temporal, and argument-gap patterns as separate steps.
Represent parallel attachment blockers and avoid false global parse certainty.
Add cycle, span, and argument-link validation.
acceptance: Each relation has separate minimal pairs and ambiguity fixtures.
Unsupported structures remain unresolved.
No unrelated construction regression is introduced.

work_items.title: Expand voice, valence and speech-act forms
work_items.objective: Separate grammatical form, semantic roles, and communicative force.
implementation_sequence: Use minimal active/passive pairs and language-specific morphology.
Add imperatives, requests, commands, and interrogatives in separately named profiles.
Keep speech-act inference distinct from predicate argument linking.
Record evidence when word order is language-specific.
acceptance: Voice and role mappings pass contrastive tests.
Speech-act force is not inferred solely from punctuation or keywords.
Unsupported profiles abstain.

work_items.title: Expand language profiles without false transfer
work_items.objective: Reuse architecture while explicitly adapting construction, morphology, order, and lexical resources for each language.
implementation_sequence: Define language-profile contract and feature inventory.
Add one language/construction profile at a time.
Require native/appropriate evidence where claims are made about native use.
Do not treat translated corpora as evidence of native syntax or discourse.
acceptance: Per-language metrics and regression suites are independent.
No language support is inherited without evidence.
Translation limitations accompany every result.

exit_gate: Every added construction has a versioned specification and independently defined fixture set.
No accepted capability regresses.
Candidate grammar remains separate until acceptance.
Supported-language scope is explicit.

phases.title: Semantic composition and canonical meaning projection
phases.objective: Improve compositional integration so accepted lexical and construction evidence can form typed, traceable semantic representations and project to canonical USG-SEM only when no meaning is lost.

work_items.title: Formalize composition interfaces between stages
work_items.objective: Define typed inputs/outputs, candidate alternatives, unresolved dependencies, and provenance propagation for each stage boundary.
implementation_sequence: Inventory current Phase 4/5 envelope and Phase 6 candidate graphs.
Define stage boundary schemas and compatibility tests.
Record resource/rule references and derivation IDs on every composed structure.
Preserve partial results without marking them complete.
acceptance: Stage outputs validate and preserve all source spans and provenance.
Unknown fields are handled by version policy, not silently discarded.
Replay produces deterministic structures.

work_items.title: Expand predicate, argument, role and relation composition
work_items.objective: Compose predicates with typed arguments, event/state participants, properties, and relations.
implementation_sequence: Reuse existing frame and role inventories.
Define domain/range constraints, required/optional roles, and role conflicts.
Add role mapping only with positive and contrastive evidence.
Represent unresolved links as candidates.
acceptance: Per-construction role/link exactness passes.
Conflicting roles remain explicit.
No role is inferred only from a lexical association score.

work_items.title: Add safe semantic projection and loss detection
work_items.objective: Project supported semantic structures into USG-SEM/1.0 without truncation or invented meaning.
implementation_sequence: Create explicit relation-to-USG-SEM projection tables.
Round-trip each supported projection through current adapters and SQLite.
Detect unmapped roles/operators/metadata and refuse lossy projection.
Retain OPAQUE payloads and candidate graphs when canonical representation is insufficient.
acceptance: Loss detector blocks all unsupported projections.
Round-trip and integrity tests pass.
Any normative contract gap routes to a separately versioned migration.

work_items.title: Integrate canonical persistence and replay
work_items.objective: Persist accepted semantic documents and full derivation metadata using the existing SQLite authority.
implementation_sequence: Use existing Phase 3 repository APIs; do not create a parallel canonical store.
Persist immutable input/run/resource/derivation references.
Test idempotence, revision history, corruption checks, replay, and index rebuild.
Keep caches and search indexes rebuildable.
acceptance: Existing Phase 3 persistence tests remain green.
Snapshot integrity and provenance survive reopen/replay.
No secondary canonical database is introduced.

exit_gate: Composition contracts are versioned.
Accepted cases preserve source-to-semantic derivations.
Projection is loss-detecting and round-trip tested.
Canonical persistence remains authoritative.

phases.title: Operator, scope, time and modality system
phases.objective: Represent how meaning is modified by negation, quantification, tense, aspect, modality, conditionals, comparison, and nested scope.

work_items.title: Create a typed operator registry
work_items.objective: Define operator identity, type, target, operand, scope, precedence/interaction, language realization, and evidence requirements.
implementation_sequence: Inventory current accepted and candidate operators.
Define typed schemas and legal target classes.
Record scope alternatives rather than collapsing ambiguous readings.
Add compatibility and serialization tests.
acceptance: Every operator is typed and source-grounded.
Invalid target/operand combinations are rejected.
Ambiguous scope remains explicit.

work_items.title: Expand negation and quantifier scope
work_items.objective: Handle nested negation and quantifier interactions with contrastive minimal pairs.
implementation_sequence: Add scope-contrast and polarity cases.
Test quantifier domain, restrictor, nuclear scope, and negation order.
Preserve unknown scope when parsing evidence is insufficient.
Link scope structure to semantic composition.
acceptance: Per-language held-out scope cases pass.
No keyword-only scope shortcut is accepted.
Abstention and alternative readings are calibrated.

work_items.title: Add tense, aspect, modality and temporal relations
work_items.objective: Represent event time, reference time, duration, completion, possibility, obligation, ability, and evidential distinctions where profiles support them.
implementation_sequence: Define temporal and modal primitives separately from lexical labels.
Map morphology and constructions to candidate operators.
Add contrastive tense/aspect/modality benchmarks.
Preserve underspecified time and modal force.
acceptance: Operator distinctions pass profile-specific tests.
Temporal inference is provenance-grounded.
No unsupported temporal fact is invented.

work_items.title: Add conditional and comparative composition
work_items.objective: Compose conditionals and comparison without treating correlation or conditional wording as causality.
implementation_sequence: Represent antecedent/consequent and comparison operands explicitly.
Test counterfactual, hypothetical, factual, and ambiguous variants.
Keep causal relations separate from conditionals unless evidence supports the relation.
Add scope and operator interaction tests.
acceptance: Contrastive and ambiguity sets pass.
No automatic causal inference from conditional form.
Canonical projection preserves all operands and scope.

exit_gate: Operator registry and scope model are versioned.
Per-operator and interaction tests pass.
Ambiguity/underspecification is preserved.
Temporal and modal claims remain bounded to evaluated profiles.

phases.title: Discourse, reference and entity tracking
phases.objective: Connect mentions across clauses and documents while distinguishing mention identity, discourse referent, concept, and real-world entity identity.

work_items.title: Build discourse mention and context records
work_items.objective: Represent mention spans, grammatical features, discourse role, salience cues, and local context.
implementation_sequence: Inventory Phase 5 discourse and Phase 6 reference candidate outputs.
Define stable mention IDs and source spans.
Record features used for retrieval separately from identity decisions.
Add sentence- and document-scope tests.
acceptance: Mention chain preserves all source references.
A mention is not treated as an entity identity.
Context window and resource versions are reproducible.

work_items.title: Rank antecedent candidates conservatively
work_items.objective: Use agreement, syntax, discourse, semantic compatibility, and context to rank plausible antecedents.
implementation_sequence: Generate multiple candidates and explicit no-antecedent option.
Evaluate against held-out coreference datasets where rights/annotation permit.
Report precision/recall and abstention by language/profile.
Do not merge entities merely because names or embeddings are similar.
acceptance: Multi-antecedent and no-antecedent tests pass.
False identity merges are measured separately.
Uncertain cases remain unresolved.

work_items.title: Add discourse relations and multi-sentence composition
work_items.objective: Represent temporal, causal, contrastive, elaboration, and reference relations only within explicit evidence boundaries.
implementation_sequence: Start with relation types already supported by contracts.
Keep discourse relation candidates distinct from truth/causal inference.
Add document-level replay and contradiction fixtures.
Expose derivation and unresolved links in diagnostics.
acceptance: Document-level tests preserve sentence boundaries and provenance.
Unsupported discourse relations abstain.
No silent cross-document identity merge.

exit_gate: Mention and entity layers are distinct.
Reference resolution reports alternatives and abstention.
Discourse relations have typed evidence and per-language tests.

phases.title: Knowledge-layer integration and contextual retrieval
phases.objective: Make the existing Phase 7 knowledge layer a reusable evidence source for interpretation and reasoning without creating a second knowledge database or turning retrieval into automatic truth.

work_items.title: Map exact runtime consumers of the Phase 7 knowledge adapter
work_items.objective: Determine which interpretation and reasoning stages actually consume the read-only adapter and what version they use.
implementation_sequence: Inspect current Phase 7 API/CLI/adapter and all intended consumers.
Add explicit integration tests; do not infer consumption from the resource map.
Record accepted-profile, candidate-opt-in, and unresolved behavior.
Publish a runtime consumption matrix.
acceptance: Every declared integration is proven by code and test evidence.
Candidate state is preserved end-to-end.
No duplicate canonical store appears.

work_items.title: Resolve concept mappings through explicit evidence workflows
work_items.objective: Reduce unresolved cross-language mappings where source evidence supports it, while preserving many-to-many and unresolved relations.
implementation_sequence: Inventory the existing 43 unresolved mappings and their evidence.
Group by concept, sense, language profile, source agreement, and rights.
Promote only mappings meeting the declared evidence gate.
Retain disagreement and ambiguous mapping alternatives.
acceptance: Every mapping has source, relation type, evidence, status, and reviewer/algorithm provenance.
No spelling/translation/similarity-only identity merge.
Unresolved remainder is reported rather than hidden.

work_items.title: Build contextual knowledge retrieval diagnostics
work_items.objective: Explain why candidate concepts/relations were retrieved and how context changed ranking.
implementation_sequence: Define context features and feature provenance.
Keep usage frequency/association score separate from truth/entailment.
Expose rejected candidates and ranking reasons.
Test domain, language, local discourse, and conflicting source scenarios.
acceptance: Retrieval results are reproducible and explainable.
False merges and over-broad associations are evaluated.
Candidate/accepted lifecycle is visible to callers.

work_items.title: Connect knowledge candidates to semantic interpretation
work_items.objective: Allow interpreters to use knowledge as a constrained candidate source without silently injecting assertions.
implementation_sequence: Add read-only candidate retrieval at explicit stage boundaries.
Use candidate values only when supported by grammar/source context.
Record knowledge version and evidence IDs in output envelope.
Require separate profile tests for accepted knowledge consumption.
acceptance: Knowledge lookups do not mutate the canonical graph.
Unsupported or conflicting retrieval yields alternatives/abstention.
Integration gains are evaluated against lexical-only baseline.

exit_gate: Runtime consumption is proven, not inferred.
Unresolved mappings remain explicit.
Knowledge retrieval is read-only and provenance-rich.
No external/candidate fact becomes canonical truth by retrieval.

phases.title: Evidence-grounded semantic reasoning and explanation
phases.objective: Extend the existing structured reasoning foundation to operate on accepted semantic documents and knowledge with derivation, evidence, conflict, scope, and bounded execution.

work_items.title: Define reasoning capability and rule dependency contracts
work_items.objective: Connect Phase 2 rule semantics with typed outputs from interpretation, persistence, and knowledge adapters.
implementation_sequence: Inventory current rule registry, execution engine, grounding, evidence assessment, and query/explanation services.
Declare input/output schemas, preconditions, resource versions, and allowed side effects.
Separate retrieval, deduction, abduction, analogy, and hypothesis generation.
Reject undeclared rule dependencies.
acceptance: Rule execution is deterministic within declared scope.
All dependencies and derivations are traceable.
Rules cannot escape their side-effect/step limits.

work_items.title: Implement support, conflict and contradiction analysis across sources
work_items.objective: Assess evidence for/against propositions without conflating source count, repetition, confidence, and truth.
implementation_sequence: Reuse evidence assessment and source provenance contracts.
Model support, contradiction, unknown, and unresolved states separately.
Deduplicate correlated sources and identify shared upstream provenance.
Test conflict, missing evidence, temporal qualification, and source reliability.
acceptance: Correlated copies do not count as independent corroboration.
Conflict is preserved and explained.
No probability/confidence is asserted without calibration evidence.

work_items.title: Add bounded multi-step inference and query explanations
work_items.objective: Answer supported semantic queries with complete proof traces and controlled execution budgets.
implementation_sequence: Define rule depth, branching, time, memory, and recursion budgets.
Return proof/derivation graph, evidence references, and failed preconditions.
Preserve unknown/undetermined rather than force yes/no.
Replay all accepted reasoning benchmarks.
acceptance: Every conclusion has a replayable derivation.
Budget exhaustion is explicit.
Negative and unknown cases are tested separately.

work_items.title: Connect document, discourse, and temporal reasoning
work_items.objective: Reason over multi-sentence semantic documents without losing scope, time, source, or referential uncertainty.
implementation_sequence: Use typed semantic graph and explicit discourse links.
Propagate time/modal scope and unresolved reference state.
Test entailment, contradiction, temporal ordering, and non-entailment.
Add evidence that distinguishes same event, related event, and coincidental co-occurrence.
acceptance: Document reasoning passes held-out independent cases.
Unsupported inference abstains.
No causal or identity inference arises from association alone.

exit_gate: Reasoning is bounded, typed, traceable, and replayable.
Evidence conflicts and unknown states are preserved.
Every accepted inference capability has independent evaluation.

phases.title: Governed autonomous development and candidate learning
phases.objective: Evolve the existing scheduled growth planner into a closed-loop development assistant that can prepare candidate improvements and deterministic repairs while preventing self-validation and unsafe semantic promotion.

work_items.title: Implement bounded deterministic repair executor
work_items.objective: Automate only low-risk test, fixture, packaging, report, documentation, and CI repairs with exact regression replay.
implementation_sequence: Use the existing growth plan as input, but require each repair to map to a known deterministic defect class.
Run in isolated branch/worktree/container with resource/time/network limits.
Run focused tests, protected regression suites, static checks, and exact replay.
Open a PR with patch, evidence, rollback, and risk classification; do not merge without the relevant repository gate.
acceptance: Only allowlisted change classes are auto-generated.
Sandbox and execution budgets are enforced.
A failing or nondeterministic repair is discarded and logged.
No semantic/runtime resource promotion occurs.

work_items.title: Add candidate construction and resource generators
work_items.objective: Generate candidate lexical, morphology, grammar, frame, and mapping proposals from measured error clusters.
implementation_sequence: Generate candidates only into isolated candidate artifacts.
Require provenance and rule/source citations for every generated record.
Deduplicate by stable identity and preserve conflicting alternatives.
Attach explicit evidence gap and proposed acceptance profile.
acceptance: Generated candidates cannot enter runtime paths.
Candidate reports are deterministic or fully seeded.
Missing evidence blocks promotion.

work_items.title: Build active evaluation and experiment selection
work_items.objective: Select the next most informative test or corpus slice using uncertainty, recurrence, coverage gaps, and cost.
implementation_sequence: Use evidence-driven planner features and separate source metrics.
Choose high-information cases without changing held-out test membership.
Record selection rationale and seed.
Keep exploration and acceptance datasets separate.
acceptance: Sampling is reproducible and does not leak held-out labels.
Selection objective is explainable.
No metric is optimized by dropping hard cases.

work_items.title: Automate candidate evaluation, decision packets and rollback
work_items.objective: Generate machine-readable accept/reject/needs-evidence packets for candidates and integrate only approved scopes.
implementation_sequence: Run per-profile acceptance gates, adversarial tests, and regression replay.
Compare to frozen baselines and report regressions.
Require independent evidence for semantic promotion.
Create versioned promotion proposal and rollback artifact.
acceptance: No self-generated oracle is accepted as independent evidence.
Promotion is a separate auditable transaction.
Rollback of resource and code versions is tested.

work_items.title: Introduce risk-tiered automation policy
work_items.objective: Allow unattended merging only for explicitly low-risk changes and retain stronger gates for semantic, contractual, and data-rights decisions.
implementation_sequence: Classify changes as docs/test/harness, deterministic infrastructure, candidate data, runtime semantics, normative contracts, or rights/policy.
Define required workflows and review/approval per tier.
Record why a tier qualifies and its rollback path.
Add tests preventing a higher-risk category from using a lower-risk merge route.
acceptance: Risk classification is machine-checkable.
Semantic/runtime/contract changes cannot be auto-promoted by generic planner output.
All automation actions have logs and rollback records.

exit_gate: Planner, candidate generator, and executor remain separate components.
Every candidate passes independent evaluation before promotion.
Auto-merge authority is limited by tested risk tier.
Self-validation loops, held-out leakage, and silent baseline changes are blocked.

phases.title: Workbench integration, release engineering and operational hardening
phases.objective: Make accepted USG capabilities usable, inspectable, portable, and maintainable as a coherent local development product.

work_items.title: Unify developer-facing run and inspection contracts
work_items.objective: Make APIs, CLI, Kernel Lab, and SDKs expose the same versioned run envelope and diagnostic vocabulary where appropriate.
implementation_sequence: Inventory current endpoints and CLI commands.
Expose input, output, resources, derivations, ambiguity, and diagnostics through versioned APIs.
Add schema validation and compatibility tests.
Keep implementation-native detail accessible.
acceptance: Every UI/API response links to exact run and resource versions.
No display-only simplification changes the underlying evidence.
Backward compatibility is tested.

work_items.title: Improve reproducibility, portability and local operation
work_items.objective: Provide one documented local install/run/test path without paid services or permanent network requirements for core tests.
implementation_sequence: Pin runtime/tool dependencies and document supported Python/Node/browser versions.
Add deterministic setup and offline fixture mode.
Make caches rebuildable and configuration explicit.
Document data/storage budgets and recovery.
acceptance: Fresh supported environment passes quickstart and test smoke suite.
Core offline tests do not call network services.
Recovery and backup paths are tested.

work_items.title: Add performance and resource-budget instrumentation
work_items.objective: Measure latency, memory, storage, cache behavior, and workflow consumption by module.
implementation_sequence: Set baseline workloads and record hardware/runtime context.
Instrument stage-level cost without changing semantics.
Define budget warnings and safe cancellation.
Optimize only after profiling and with semantic regression replay.
acceptance: Performance reports are reproducible.
Resource limits fail safely.
Optimization preserves exact acceptance behavior.

work_items.title: Publish versioned releases and compatibility policy
work_items.objective: Coordinate schemas, adapters, implementation releases, and migrations through a clear compatibility matrix.
implementation_sequence: Define versioning policy for contracts, adapters, resource bundles, and Workbench releases.
Generate release notes from accepted change records.
Document deprecation windows and migration tools.
Keep archives immutable.
acceptance: Every release maps code/resource/contract versions.
Migrations have compatibility and rollback tests.
No silent schema drift.

exit_gate: Developer experience works from clean setup.
APIs/CLI/UI expose provenance and diagnostics consistently.
Performance and compatibility are measured.
Release artifacts are reproducible and recoverable.

phases.title: Optional multimodal and grounded-world research horizon
phases.objective: Explore how the semantic architecture might extend to visual, audio, temporal, and action/event evidence after text profiles and provenance/evaluation controls are sufficiently reliable.

work_items.title: Define modality-neutral evidence and alignment requirements
work_items.objective: Research typed links between text spans, image regions, audio intervals, video frames, and external observations.
implementation_sequence: Review canonical contract capabilities and extension limits.
Prototype out-of-band evidence references without changing USG-SEM/1.0.
Specify timestamp, coordinate, sampling, and source provenance rules.
Evaluate lossless preservation and ambiguity.
acceptance: A separate research report demonstrates value and contract fit.
No normative schema change occurs implicitly.
Modality-specific evidence is not treated as verified truth.

work_items.title: Run one bounded multimodal pilot only after evidence readiness
work_items.objective: Test one narrow modality/semantic relation pair using a rights-cleared, independently evaluated dataset.
implementation_sequence: Choose modality and task using explicit capability gap and cost analysis.
Build a separate adapter and candidate path.
Create independent evaluation and privacy/security controls.
Compare against text-only baseline.
acceptance: Pilot has independent evidence, exact limits, and a rollback path.
No broad multimodal capability claim is made.
The pilot is not a prerequisite for core text system progress.

exit_gate: Exploratory evidence justifies the next work.
Text-first architecture remains stable.
Rights, privacy, and evaluation are independently accepted.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Normative contracts and migrations
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: Any change to USG-SEM/1.0 or accepted output semantics requires a dedicated versioned migration, compatibility adapter, conformance suite, and rollback record.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Evidence and dataset governance
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: Every dataset/resource records source, license, rights status, population, language/profile, retrieval time, transformations, digest, and intended use.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Security and privacy
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: External text and generated artifacts are untrusted data; sanitize workflow output; never execute retrieved content; minimize personal data; isolate untrusted candidate files and generated code.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Observability and provenance
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: Every stage emits structured diagnostics and stable provenance links; missing evidence is not zero; errors are categorized by source.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Documentation and usability
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: Every implementation PR updates the relevant technical doc, central documentation hub, tests, resource manifest, and README when the major status changes.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Cost and operational limits
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: Prefer local deterministic paths, resumable workflows, bounded budgets, artifact retention, caching, and optional network access; no required paid dependency for core tests.

cross_cutting_workstreams.name: Rollback and frozen baselines
cross_cutting_workstreams.rule: Protect accepted behavior with immutable baseline artifacts; baseline changes require explicit evidence-backed versioning.

maturity_gates.name: Reliable bounded components
maturity_gates.condition: Contracts, stage outputs, and source provenance are deterministic and testable.

maturity_gates.name: Reproducible cross-runtime behavior
maturity_gates.condition: Specific shared profiles pass common fixtures across implementations; differences remain explicit.

maturity_gates.name: Independently evaluated construction coverage
maturity_gates.condition: Each claimed construction has rights-cleared, held-out, per-language evidence and calibrated abstention.

maturity_gates.name: Compositional document understanding
maturity_gates.condition: Multiple constructions, operators, and discourse references compose into loss-aware semantic documents.

maturity_gates.name: Evidence-grounded knowledge and reasoning
maturity_gates.condition: Read-only knowledge retrieval and bounded inference provide traceable derivations and preserve conflict/unknown.

maturity_gates.name: Governed continuous improvement
maturity_gates.condition: Candidate generation, sandboxing, evaluation, acceptance, replay, rollback, and risk-tiered automation operate without self-validation.

maturity_gates.name: Optional broader modalities and deployments
maturity_gates.condition: Only pursued when core text evidence and operational maturity justify the added complexity.

factors: number and importance of affected supported profiles
availability of a valid acceptance oracle
risk to accepted behavior, rights, privacy, and contracts
rules: Prefer fixing the earliest evidenced blocker over adding downstream heuristics.
Prefer a small construction with an independent acceptance path over a broad feature with no reliable oracle.
Do not promote work solely because a model proposes it or a workflow passes.
Keep separate metrics for candidate coverage, parse correctness, semantic correctness, abstention, and execution reliability.
Prefer work that reduces uncertainty and unblocks multiple later tasks, but do not collapse trade-offs into a hidden score.

execution_packet_contract: Stable packet ID and one bounded objective.
Exact linked failure cases, plan items, source commits, resource versions, and language profiles.
Preconditions and dependencies checked against current main before coding.
Target files/modules and minimal implementation sequence.
Positive, negative, ambiguous, boundary, adversarial, and compatibility tests as applicable.
Acceptance thresholds fixed before the final held-out run.
Explicit not-in-scope items and runtime/candidate/contract mutation classification.
Reproducible artifacts and exact commit/run references.
Machine-readable completion state updated only from authoritative evidence.

automatic_updates: phase status snapshots from the current source registry
linked SYS backlog status snapshots from the backlog implementation table
safety_rules: A PR merge does not automatically mark a semantic capability accepted.
Only explicit machine-readable acceptance artifacts can mark a scope accepted.
Missing or unparsable source states are reported as unavailable; they are never guessed.
The synchronizer does not edit the strategic plan or source-of-truth trackers.
Generated status refreshes are proposed through a pull request; future phase work remains unstarted until explicitly scheduled.

sources_of_truth.purpose: Current phase status and registered evidence-source families.
Declared phase/source dependencies and prohibited use modes.
SYS work-item dependencies, completion scope, and next execution sequence.
Open Phase 6 continuation items and their candidate/acceptance state.
Phase 7 bounded acceptance and knowledge-layer capability boundary.
Phase 8 scope, automatic acceptance protocol, and formal decision boundary.
Historical diagnostic baseline; use newer trackers for later progress.
Latest append-only system evidence snapshots and Phase 8 acceptance artifacts.
